findings.reviewed_statement: Most adults need at least 2,000 mg/day sodium.
findings.comparator: Adult sodium AI is 1,500 mg/day; CDRR advises reducing intake if above 2,300 mg/day. A general 2,000 mg minimum for most adults is not established.
findings.recommendation: Remove the generalized 2,000 mg minimum unless a separate population-specific source is supplied.

findings.reviewed_statement: Calcium age/sex grouping is combined in a way that obscures adult men 19–50 and the 71+ grouping.
Po is used as a potassium symbol.
findings.comparator: Potassium is K; Po is polonium.
findings.recommendation: Use potassium (K) and spell out vitamin K when distinction is needed.

findings.reviewed_statement: Water-soluble vitamins cannot be stored by the body.
findings.comparator: Vitamin B12 is water-soluble but stored in very large amounts relative to daily intake.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the statement and note B12 as an important exception.

findings.reviewed_statement: Vitamin A values shown as mcg without RAE.
findings.comparator: NIH ODS expresses recommendations in mcg RAE.

findings.reviewed_statement: Folate shown as 400 mcg without DFE.
findings.comparator: Adult folate recommendation is 400 mcg DFE.
findings.recommendation: Use mcg DFE and distinguish folic acid from food folate where relevant.

findings.reviewed_statement: Niacin values shown as mg without NE.
findings.comparator: Adult niacin recommendations are expressed as mg NE.

findings.reviewed_statement: Vitamin D shown only as 600 IU and 800 IU age 71+.
findings.comparator: Adults 19–70: 15 mcg (600 IU); adults 71+: 20 mcg (800 IU).
findings.recommendation: Retain the values but present both mcg and IU.
